title: Replay harness with weighted sampling for embedding + reranker regression detection
creator: Lina Chen
description:
Goal: Build a replay-based batch evaluation harness that runs whenever a model binary or serving config changes, using weighted sampling of historical traffic to surface precision/recall deltas and distributional drift for embedding+reranker pipelines. This ticket covers design and MVP implementation for nightly and on-change runs, metrics aggregation, and an alerting threshold framework.

Why: We need deterministic, explainable signals tied to model/config diffs so PMs and SREs can decide whether a rollout is safe. Online canary checks are useful but slow to converge; a targeted replay on representative historical traces gives faster, reproducible regressions and concrete examples for root cause.

Scope (MVP):
- Replay engine that consumes archived request traces (JSONL) and replays through current and candidate model/config variants in batch.
- Weighted sampling strategy: upweight recent traffic and low-frequency query buckets so we surface regressions that affect tail use cases. Sampling configuration should be pluggable.
- Compute per-query pairwise rerank metrics: top-k recall@k (1,3,5), mean reciprocal rank (MRR), normalized discounted cumulative gain (nDCG) for ranking outputs produced by reranker; cosine/similarity shifts for embeddings.
- Delta aggregation with confidence intervals (bootstrap) and per-segment breakdowns (region, device class, customer tier).
- Failure examples: save top N divergent examples with full inputs, outputs, scores, and token/embedding diffs to a short-lived artifact store for inspection.
- Integration points: webhook to alerting/console and a summary artifact (s3) that the Console can pick up for a change UI.

Non-goals (MVP):
- Full streaming/real-time shadowing.
- Automated rollback.

Acceptance criteria:
- Replay job runs automatically when model or serving config is tagged for rollout (manual trigger also supported).
- Generates a human-readable summary with delta metrics and top-10 regression examples uploaded to s3 and linked in the Linear ticket.
- Alerts fire when delta MRR decreases by >3% with p < 0.05 (configurable).
- Sampling config can be tuned without code changes (yaml + examples).
- End-to-end run for a small historical trace (10k requests) completes in < 90 minutes on dev infra.

Design notes / trade-offs:
- Deterministic replay vs. freshness: archived traces give reproducibility but may miss emergent patterns. We bias sampling toward recent traces to partially mitigate.
- Weighted sampling schema: score = alpha * recency_rank + beta * inverse-frequency_bucket + gamma * customer_tier_weight. Default alpha/beta/gamma chosen empirically; tuning via small grid search.
- Metrics computation: bootstrap-based CIs preferred for small sample segments; approximate variance formulas for large runs to save compute.
- Storage: artifacts to s3 with 30d retention; full dump optional (off by default) to avoid S3 cost blowup.

Implementation plan:
1) Trace ingestion and lightweight indexer (week 1) - parse JSONL traces and compute attributes used for sampling.
2) Replay engine (week 2) - parallel runner that can call current and candidate model endpoints (local or hosted) and capture outputs.
3) Metrics library (week 2-3) - implement recall@k, MRR, nDCG, embedding shift metrics, bootstrap CI.
4) Aggregation + artifact writer (week 3) - produce summary JSON and top-N examples, upload to s3.
5) Console hook + alerting (week 4) - simple webhook + threshold config.

Telemetry and alerts:
- Primary signals: delta MRR, delta recall@1/3/5, mean embedding cosine shift.
- Per-segment breakdowns: continent, traffic bucket, customer_tier.
- Alert if any primary signal crosses configured thresholds for two consecutive runs.
- Log job runtime, error rates, and per-call latency to help identify infra issues.

Testing strategy:
- Unit tests for sampling and metrics.
- Synthetic trace generator to produce controlled regressions for end-to-end tests.
- Run against a previously recorded rollout that had a known regression to validate detection sensitivity.

Risks / mitigation:
- Large trace replays could be costly: mitigate via sample budgets and dev quotas.
- False positives from sample noise: use bootstrap CIs and require sustained signal across runs.

Docs & artifacts:
- Design doc: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1ReplayEvalDesign (internal)
- PR (WIP): https://github.com/redwood-inference/replay-eval/pull/1234
